current_example.title: Example: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm

q-2202.name: Question 1
q-2202.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =4\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =4\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =2{u}^{2}+C \\  & =2{ln}^{2}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

2ln⁡x+C

2ln2⁡x+C

q-13813.name: Question 2
q-13813.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =6\int \frac{1}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =6\int \frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6\cdot {u}^{-1}+C \\  & =-\frac{6}{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate the integral ∫6xln2⁡xdx.

a
 −6ln2⁡x+C
b
 1ln⁡x+C
c
 6ln2⁡x+C
d
 −6ln⁡x+C
e
 6ln⁡x+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's set u=ln⁡x. Then, we have dudx=1x⟹du=1xdx.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of u and evaluate:

∫6xln2⁡xdx=6∫1(ln⁡x)2⋅dxx=6∫1u2du=−6⋅u−1+C=−6u+C=−6ln⁡x+C

q-2380.name: Question 3
q-2380.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =2\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+C\end{aligned}

Question 3
?

Calculate the integral ∫1xln⁡xdx.

a
ln⁡(ln⁡x)x+C
b
ln⁡xx+C
c
1ln⁡(ln⁡x)+C
d
ln⁡x+C
e
2ln⁡x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's set u=ln⁡x. Then, we have dudx=1x⟹du=dxx.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of u and evaluate:

∫1xln⁡xdx=∫1ln⁡x⋅dxx=∫1u⋅du=∫u−1/2du=2u1/2+C=2ln⁡x+C

q-13802.name: Question 4
q-13802.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-2194.name: Question 5
q-2194.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\sqrt{2}\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{ln}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-2194.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate the integral ∫2xln⁡xdx.

a
xln⁡(ln⁡2)+C
b
1ln⁡|ln⁡x|+C
c
2ln⁡|ln⁡x|+C
d
2ln⁡|ln⁡x|+C
e
ln⁡|ln⁡x|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's set u=ln⁡x. Then, we have dudx=1x⟹du=1xdx.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of u and evaluate:

∫2xln⁡xdx=2∫1ln⁡x⋅dxx=2∫1u⋅du=2ln⁡|u|+C=2ln⁡|ln⁡x|+C
